subject: Next steps: Lobelia private deployment security intake & air-gap feasibility

Subject: Next steps: Lobelia private deployment security intake & air-gap feasibility

Hi Anita / Lobelia security team,

Thanks again for taking time today — appreciate the clear rundown of Lobelia's regulatory requirements. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Summary of what we discussed
- Compliance posture: Lobelia is pursuing HIPAA for PHI flows and has GDPR obligations for EU patients.
- SOC 2: current internal scope covers application & infra; you requested evidence of our SOC 2 controls for data-in-transit and tenant isolation.
- Deployment model: you're evaluating a private VPC (customer-managed VPC peering) and a potential air-gapped on-prem option for some workloads.
- Network: key ask was separation between inference-serving subnets and any shared management plane, and whether KV caches persist off-GPU.

Proposed immediate next steps
1) I attached a short vendor questionnaire (lobelia_security_questionnaire_v1.xlsx) — if you can populate the sections marked Security/Network/Compliance we can triage answers and return scope-bound evidence.
2) We'll provide our SOC 2 summary (redwood-soc2-summary.pdf) and a private-deploy network sketch with separation options (hand-drawn-network-sketch.png).
3) Marissa will set up a technical deep-dive with our infra/security engineer to go through the network isolation and air-gap feasibility (30–45m).
4) If procurement needs contract language or timelines, loop in procurement@lobeliahealth.com and we’ll share SOW/CDP timelines.

Timing: can we aim to get the questionnaire back by EOD Wednesday (Sep 22)? That will let us schedule the deep-dive later that week.

Attachments: lobelia_security_questionnaire_v1.xlsx (please fill), redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (confidential controls summary), hand-drawn-network-sketch.png (initial options).

Thanks — happy to reassign or clarify any section.

Best,

Thanks Michael — good summary. A couple clarifying items from our side before we return the questionnaire: 

1) SOC 2 scope: when you say "controls for data-in-transit and tenant isolation" can you confirm whether your SOC 2 report covers managed infrastructure (Redwood-hosted control plane) or only the hosted service? Our auditors will need to understand where responsibilities sit if we go with a private VPC deployment.

2) Air-gap: the use case we flagged is for a subset of PII workloads where we cannot have any egress. Can Redwood support a fully air-gapped appliance that never receives patches from the internet, and if so, what is your recommended patch workflow?

3) Network diagram: the sketch will help but can you also indicate if KV cache is stored on durable media or ephemeral GPU memory? That affects our data persistence assessment.

We will try to fill the questionnaire by Wed (our EOD is 9/22) but if we need more time we will let you know. Also copying procurement for timeline visibility.

-Anita
Anita Rao
Head of Security Operations
Lobelia Health

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2027 12:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps: Lobelia private deployment security intake & air-gap feasibility

Hi Anita — quick answers to the checklist items before we do the deep-dive: 

- SOC 2: our SOC 2 Type II covers the Redwood Hosted control plane and the managed inference service. For Private/VPC deployments we provide a SOC 2 summary that maps each control to the private deployment model; where control ownership shifts to customer-managed infra we note that as shared responsibility. We will attach the mapping doc to the Drive link.

- Air-gapped option: we have an on-prem package used by other customers that can be deployed without outbound internet access. Patching is supported via air-gap update bundles delivered by secure media (customer-initiated). For high-risk patches we recommend a scheduled maintenance window that your infra team controls. We will outline the patch cadence and operational steps in the working session.

- KV cache persistence: by default KV cache is ephemeral and kept in GPU memory and local SSD cache for warm restarts; we do not persist decrypted KV to remote durable storage in the standard private deploy. If you require zero-durable persistence we can present a configuration option that avoids SSD writeback.

Attached: hand-drawn-network-sketch.png (simple layout showing isolated inference subnets + optional air-gapped appliance). I also uploaded a short SOC 2 summary to the shared Drive (link below).

Proposed next action: Michael / Anita — pick two slots for a 45-minute technical session and we’ll have Neha (our security lead) and an infra engineer on the call.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0Bz-example/redwood-lobelia
